scenario: Waking up to find that a major home appliance has been malfunctioning for a while and now has broken down completely.
Looking at a work dashboard where the key performance indicator is consistently trending below the target line for the third month in a row.
Walking past a hardware store where signs indicate a 20% price increase on all essential tools starting tomorrow.
Receiving a notification that a bank account fee structure has changed, increasing costs for multiple services held at that institution.
Sitting in a doctor's waiting room while the clock ticks by, aware that a routine endoscopy is scheduled for later this morning.
Scanning a grocery receipt to realize the monthly food bill is significantly higher than the previous month.
Rolling dice in a board game and landing on a space that involves a direct monetary penalty.
Reading a construction cost estimate where the total expenditure exceeds the originally signed contract amount.
Watching the battery percentage on a smartphone drop to 3% moments before a large file download begins.
Arriving at a nail salon to find that the specific shade of polish required has been discontinued by the manufacturer.
Looking at a weather forecast that predicts persistent overcast skies and a 60% chance of rain for the entire week.
Receiving a letter from the tax authority notifying that an additional 15% deposit is due by next month.
Checking a medical bill where the remitted amount by the insurer is less than the billed amount.
Attempting to access a file on the main hard drive only to find that a diagnosis marker appears, preventing read access.
Standing at the kitchen counter yesterday evening with an empty bag of coffee beans, knowing the daily supply is gone.
Receiving an email from a supplier stating that a critical hardware component is backordered for four weeks.
Sorting through a wardrobe on a Tuesday and finding that the only surviving hem of the trousers wears a tear.
Watching the stock market index dip 2% while listening to a newsletter argue that the crash is structural.
Walking into a dental clinic with a broken tooth, asking to measure chart lines and x-rays during the appointment.
Attempting to bake bread, only to find the yeast has passed its expiration date and the recipe requires active culture.
Listening to the radio on a highway while accustomed to hearing that traffic incidents are "unresolvable."
Logging into a video call to find the microphone settings are disabled, requiring a laptop restart and reconnect.
Standing in line at a bakery where the counter is closed and the waiter says the chocolate cake is gone.
Reviewing a college board decision where the application status has shifted to Waitlist.
Opening a package from a delivery service to find that the item inside the bubble wrap is scratched.
Trying to make a coffee before work, realizing the filter has stopped being produced by the manufacturer.
Avoiding in front of a wall of pinned delivery bag tags, observing a red border over one of them.
Navigating a subway in Tokyo with the announcement indicating the next train is arriving in 30 minutes.
Opening a folder on a drop drive to find 14 photos missing a crucial timestamp.
Assessing a wooden dock before stepping onto it, noting several splintered guard rails have collapsed.
Going to a hardware store to buy planks for a shelf, encountering a stock shortage of the exact length needed.
Scratching a winning lottery number on a scratch card with zero agreement to the numbers selected.
Opening a mailbox to find a parking ticket and a water damage invoice in the same envelope.
Following a trail through a park and noticing an unexpected bird nesting on a fence post.
Reading a company newsletter confirming that the pier event is delayed by one week due to weather.
Checking a flight status website where a due to airport strike causes a delay notice of four hours.
Looking at a calendar where an unanswered phone call reminder flashes in red.
Spinning a roulette wheel and watching the ball carafe hit the half-green space twice in a row.
Standing at a crosswalk with a flashing light where one foot hits the red walk signal and the other still shows green.
Comparing a reading notebook to a publishing spec sheet and noticing the third outcome is ambiguous.
Watching the drip of a ceiling pipe into a bucket at a non-2g/24hr rejection notice.
Opening a sits-up bulletin board at the local church, watching barber tape pull from a rip.
Staring at a laptop screen where a thumbnail says "do not eat this fish."
Rewatching 13 clips to a public project, hearing the old loop of a broken tunnel.
Playing a lottery for a draw, noticing that the eight-slot tetris seal flap peels off in a diagonal.
Seeing a garden sign at a park that says "Graffiti risk," facing a numbered peg at the center.
Listening to a music set where a broken scratching turntable leans to one side at the ticket booth.
Pressing a button at a transit stop where an electronic metering circuit makes an 8-hour buffer.
Looking at a health update in a clinic where a vaccine authorization has missed last year's deadline.
Checking a garden gate at a vineyard where a 12-meter address meter shows no live voltage.
